function.name: xerj_search
function.description: Run a lexical / structured search against a XERJ index using the Elasticsearch-compatible Query DSL. Use for keyword, phrase, boolean, range, and term filtering when you already know the fields and values. Maps to POST /{index}/_search on the XERJ REST API (port 9200); the `query` object is passed through verbatim as the ES `query` clause.

index.description: Name of the XERJ index (single, comma-separated list, or wildcard like "logs-*").

query.description: An Elasticsearch Query DSL clause, e.g. {"match":{"title":"quarterly report"}}, {"term":{"status":"open"}}, {"range":{"price":{"gte":10}}}, or {"bool":{"must":[...],"filter":[...]}}. Sent unchanged as the request body's `query`.

size.description: Maximum number of hits to return. Defaults to 10.

from.description: Offset of the first hit, for pagination. Defaults to 0.

sort.description: Optional ES sort spec, e.g. [{"timestamp":"desc"}]. Omit for relevance order.

source.description: Controls returned `_source` fields: true/false for all, or an array of field names.

aggs.description: Optional ES aggregations object. Not supported together with hybrid-fusion queries.

track_total_hits.description: true for an exact total hit count, false for a fast approximate count, or an integer cap.

rerank.description: Optional second-stage reranking. Maps to the request body's `rerank` field. XERJ sends the text of the top `window` hits plus the question to an external relevance model, which returns a calibrated probability (0..1) per document; hits are reordered by it, that probability REPLACES `_score`, and `min_score` prunes by it. WORTH IT WHEN: a natural-language question over prose where the right document is probably in the top 30 but not at the top, or you need an absolute relevance cut-off rather than a relative rank. NOT WORTH IT FOR: exact identifier lookups, filters, sorted or aggregation-only requests - it adds a paid network round-trip per search. NEEDS A CONFIGURED PROVIDER: the node's operator must have set a provider key (`[rerank] api_key` or TYPESAFE_API_KEY); you cannot supply one in the call. Without it the search fails with HTTP 503 `rerank_exception` - do not retry, repeat the search without `rerank`. HTTP 403 means the operator disabled it. PRIVACY: this is the only search-time feature that sends document text off the node. Proxy embeddings (`[embedding] default_endpoint`) and the WAL tap also send text off the node when an operator configures them, so never tell a user that nothing else leaves the machine. Only fields the response returns are sent, so `source` filtering also limits what leaves. Pass {} for defaults, or: `query` (string: the natural-language question to judge against; REQUIRED when the search `query` is a `bool`, a `knn` or anything else with no single question in it, otherwise read from `match`, `match_phrase`, `multi_match`, `semantic` or `simple_query_string`); `window` (int, default 30, max 300 - every judged document is paid, and `from`+`size` must fit inside it); `min_score` (0..1); `fields` (string[], exhaustive list of returned fields to send); `instructions` (string); `timeout_ms` (int, default 10000); `model` (string). Cannot be combined with `sort`, `search_after`, `collapse`, scroll or `size: 0`. READ THE RESPONSE'S `_rerank` BLOCK: `applied: true` means the order is the judge's and every `_score` is a probability or null (a hit with no verdict, counted in `unjudged`, sorts last); `applied: false` means the provider missed the deadline or answered nothing usable, and the engine's own order and scores were returned, with the cause in `reason`. Ranking quality with the provider's model has not been verified by the XERJ project.

function.name: xerj_semantic_search
function.description: Search a XERJ index by meaning over a `semantic_text` field. XERJ embeds the query server-side with its built-in embedder (no external key) and ranks by vector similarity. Maps to POST /{index}/_search with body {"query":{"semantic":{"field":...,"query":...,"k":...}}}. Use for natural-language recall and RAG retrieval.

index.description: Name of the XERJ index to search.

field.description: The `semantic_text` field to match. Must be mapped as `semantic_text` so XERJ auto-embedded it at ingest.

query.description: Natural-language query text; embedded server-side and matched by similarity.

k.description: Number of nearest neighbours to retrieve. Defaults to 10.

filter.description: Optional ES query clause pre-filter, e.g. {"term":{"category":"docs"}}. Narrows candidates without scoring.

size.description: Maximum hits to return in the response (independent of k). Defaults to 10.

function.name: xerj_vector_search
function.description: Run a k-nearest-neighbour search over a `dense_vector` field with a caller-supplied embedding. Unfiltered kNN on a full-precision cosine field (>=1,024 docs) is HNSW-served (approximate) with exact rescoring — measured recall@10 1.00 on the official bench query, 100-probe mean 0.976; num_candidates sets the beam width (floored at 800). Filtered kNN, non-cosine metrics, SQ8 fields, and small indexes run an exact brute-force scan (recall 1.00). Maps to POST /{index}/_search with the top-level `knn` clause. Use when you already have a query embedding.

index.description: Name of the XERJ index to search.

field.description: The `dense_vector` field; its dimension must match `query_vector`'s length.

query_vector.description: Query embedding as a flat array of numbers, length equal to the field's mapped dimension.

k.description: Number of nearest neighbours to return. Defaults to 10.

num_candidates.description: Optional candidate-pool size before selecting top k. On the HNSW-served (unfiltered) path this is the ANN beam width (floored at 800); on the exact filtered scan it has no effect on results.

filter.description: Optional ES query clause used as a kNN pre-filter, e.g. {"term":{"lang":"en"}}.

size.description: Maximum hits to return in the response. Defaults to 10.

function.name: xerj_hybrid_search
function.description: Fuse two or more sub-queries (e.g. a lexical BM25 query and a semantic/vector query) into one ranked result set. Maps to POST /{index}/_search with body {"query":{"hybrid":{"queries":[{"query":{...},"weight":...}],"fusion":"rrf"}}}. Fusion is "rrf" (default) or "linear"; the "learned" strategy is not implemented and errors. Aggregations cannot be combined with a hybrid query.

index.description: Name of the XERJ index to search.

queries.description: Sub-queries to fuse; each has a `query` (any XERJ/ES clause including `semantic` or `knn`) and an optional `weight`.

query.description: A XERJ/Elasticsearch query clause, e.g. {"match":{"body":"vpn outage"}} or {"semantic":{"field":"body","query":"vpn outage","k":50}}.

weight.description: Relative weight in fusion. Defaults to 1.0.

fusion.description: Fusion strategy: "rrf" (reciprocal rank fusion, default) or "linear" (weighted sum of normalized scores). "learned" is unsupported and returns an error.

rrf_k.description: Rank constant for RRF (only when fusion is "rrf"). Defaults to 60. Maps to fusion {"type":"rrf","k":<rrf_k>}.

size.description: Maximum number of fused hits to return. Defaults to 10.

rerank.description: Optional second-stage reranking. Maps to the request body's `rerank` field. XERJ sends the text of the top `window` hits plus the question to an external relevance model, which returns a calibrated probability (0..1) per document; hits are reordered by it, that probability REPLACES `_score`, and `min_score` prunes by it. WORTH IT WHEN: a natural-language question over prose where the right document is probably in the top 30 but not at the top, or you need an absolute relevance cut-off rather than a relative rank. NOT WORTH IT FOR: exact identifier lookups, filters, sorted or aggregation-only requests - it adds a paid network round-trip per search. NEEDS A CONFIGURED PROVIDER: the node's operator must have set a provider key (`[rerank] api_key` or TYPESAFE_API_KEY); you cannot supply one in the call. Without it the search fails with HTTP 503 `rerank_exception` - do not retry, repeat the search without `rerank`. HTTP 403 means the operator disabled it. Proxy embeddings (`[embedding] default_endpoint`) and the WAL tap also send text off the node when an operator configures them, so never tell a user that nothing else leaves the machine. Only fields the response returns are sent, so `source` filtering also limits what leaves. Pass {} for defaults, or: `query` (string, REQUIRED for this tool: a hybrid search has several sub-queries and no single question); `window` (int, default 30, max 300 - every judged document is paid, and `from`+`size` must fit inside it); `min_score` (0..1); `fields` (string[], exhaustive list of returned fields to send); `instructions` (string); `timeout_ms` (int, default 10000); `model` (string). Ranking quality with the provider's model has not been verified by the XERJ project.

function.name: xerj_memory_store
function.description: Persist a memory into a namespaced XERJ agent-memory store. Maps to POST /_memory/{namespace}; the text is stored in a `semantic_text` field and auto-embedded by XERJ's built-in embedder so it is recallable by meaning with no external embedding service. Namespaces isolate memories. Optionally supply a precomputed vector, metadata, an explicit id, and opt-in semantic dedup.

namespace.description: Memory namespace (isolation boundary). Starts with a lowercase letter or digit; allowed chars a-z 0-9 _ - . (max 200).

text.description: The memory text. Indexed for BM25 and auto-embedded for semantic recall.

metadata.description: Optional arbitrary metadata (tags, source, timestamps). Recall can pre-filter under the `metadata.` prefix.

vector.description: Optional caller-supplied embedding, stored as a `dense_vector` to enable kNN recall.

id.description: Optional explicit ID; a UUID is generated when omitted.

dedup.description: When true, skip the write if the nearest existing memory's similarity meets `dedup_threshold`. Defaults to false.

dedup_threshold.description: Cosine-similarity threshold in [0,1] for dedup. Defaults to 0.95. Ignored unless dedup is true.

function.name: xerj_memory_recall
function.description: Recall the most relevant memories from a namespaced XERJ store. Maps to POST /_memory/{namespace}/_recall. Three modes by input: pass `vector` for kNN over your own embedding; set `semantic: true` with `query` for server-side embedded recall (no external key); or pass just `query` for BM25 recall. Returns {"hits":[{"id","text","metadata","score"}],"namespace"}.

namespace.description: Namespace to recall from. Unknown namespace returns an empty hit list.

query.description: Query text for BM25 recall, or the string embedded server-side when `semantic` is true (required in semantic mode).

vector.description: Optional query embedding; runs kNN over stored vectors and takes precedence over query/semantic.

semantic.description: When true, XERJ embeds `query` server-side and recalls by similarity. Requires non-empty `query`. Ignored when `vector` is given. Defaults to false.

k.description: Number of memories to return. Defaults to 10.

filter.description: Optional ES query clause pre-filter over metadata, e.g. {"term":{"metadata.topic":"cats"}}.

recency_weight.description: Optional recency blend in [0,1]. 0 = pure relevance (default when omitted), 1 = pure recency.
